name: Goreback
description: A brutal stimulant-analgesic combination synthesized from industrial epinephrine analogs, topical anesthetic compounds stripped from expired dental supplies, and a proprietary compound Huit claims comes from modified livestock antibiotics. Goreback is specifically designed for combat and violence — it suppresses pain, spikes aggression and physical output, and keeps you functional through injuries that would otherwise drop you. It's named for the moment when a fighter who should be down gets back up.
effects: dramatic increase in strength and aggression
ability to continue functioning through severe physical trauma
tunnel vision focus on immediate physical threat
side_effects: inability to assess the severity of your own injuries — users die from wounds they didn't know were fatal
extreme aggression that does not discriminate between threats and allies
cardiac events from sustained epinephrine-analog load
crash: sudden total system shutdown when drug clears — dangerous if still in a combat situation
cultural_context: Goreback is the drug of the Shelf's violence economy — used by enforcers, gang soldiers, pit fighters, and anyone who needs to survive a situation that should kill them. Huit is known personally to most of the Shelf's fighting community and is reportedly protected by multiple factions simultaneously. The drug has a grim reputation even among people who use it: 'Goreback keeps you up long enough to die standing.'
story_hooks: Huit has been kidnapped — multiple factions want exclusive supply rights to Goreback, and the bidding war is getting bloody

A Shelf enforcer survived injuries that genuinely should have been fatal, and now that the Goreback has worn off, they're slowly realizing just how badly they're hurt — they need medical help but their employer can't know they're compromised
Someone is distributing military-grade Goreback analogs on the Shelf at street prices — the quality is too high for a Shelf lab, suggesting a military or corporate supply chain has been breached
